record.original_question: For commuting k-tuples of circle diffeomorphisms with rotation numbers (α1,…,αk), determine exactly the global and local arithmetic classes C^k_{r,s} and C^{k,loc}_{r,s} for C^r-to-C^s linearization.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ denote the circle, and for $\beta \in \{r, s\}$ with $1 \le s \le r \le \infty$ or $r = s = \omega$, let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\beta}_+(\mathbb{T})$ denote the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}$ of class $C^{\beta}$ (with $C^{\omega}$ meaning real-analytic). For $\alpha \in \mathbb{T}$, let $R_\alpha \colon x \mapsto x + \alpha$ be the rigid rotation by $\alpha$, and for $F \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\beta}_+(\mathbb{T})$ let $\rho(F) \in \mathbb{T}$ denote its rotation number.

Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and exponents $1 \le s \le r \le \infty$ (or $r = s = \omega$). Define the global arithmetic class
$$
C^{k}_{r,s} = \{(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k) \in \mathbb{T}^k : \text{every commuting $k$-tuple } (F_1,\dots,F_k) \in (\mathrm{Diff}^{r}_+(\mathbb{T}))^k$$
$$\text{with } F_i F_j = F_j F_i \text{ and } \rho(F_i) = \alpha_i,\ 1 \le i \le k,\text{ is simultaneously } C^{s}\text{-linearizable}\},
$$
i.e.\ there exists $h \in \mathrm{Diff}^{s}_+(\mathbb{T})$ with $h F_i h^{-1} = R_{\alpha_i}$ for all $i$. Define the local arithmetic class $C^{k,\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s} \subseteq \mathbb{T}^k$ by the same condition restricted to commuting $k$-tuples for which each $F_i \circ R_{\alpha_i}^{-1}$ is sufficiently $C^{r}$-close to the identity.

Determine the sets $C^{k}_{r,s}$ and $C^{k,\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ explicitly in arithmetic terms (for all admissible pairs $(r,s)$ and all $k \ge 1$).
artifact.status_search_result: Fayad and Khanin (Annals of Math., 2009) proved that any finite tuple of commuting C^∞ circle diffeomorphisms whose rotation numbers satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition is C^∞-conjugate to rotations, giving a sufficient arithmetic condition for the smooth case. However, exact characterizations of the classes C^k_{r,s} and C^{k,loc}_{r,s} for all regularity pairs (including the analytic case and finite differentiability) are not fully established, so the determination problem in its full generality remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Smooth linearization of commuting circle diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: A finite number of commuting diffeomorphisms with simultaneously Diophantine rotation numbers are smoothly conjugated to rotations.
status_evidence.claim: Fayad–Khanin establish a sufficient simultaneous Diophantine condition for smooth simultaneous linearization, partially resolving the determination of C^k_{r,s}.

status_evidence.title: Jean-Christophe Yoccoz and the theory of circle diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses arithmetic conditions for linearization of commuting circle diffeomorphisms and remaining open questions.
status_evidence.claim: The exact arithmetic characterization of linearizability classes for Z^k actions remains an active open problem.
